The strongest direct anchor is Nelnet because its disclosed segments explicitly include Loan Servicing and Systems plus Education Technology Services and Payments. The discovery lane includes Flywire for higher-ed payment workflow software, Maximus through Aidvantage federal loan servicing, and SLM as a credit-heavy but direct private student-loan originator/servicer. Pure lenders are included cautiously because the Serenity hypothesis seeks separable servicing/software economics rather than credit exposure. Layer 1B expansion found a small set of US-listed companies with plausible exposure to regulated student-loan servicing, campus payments, tuition billing, borrower communications, and higher-education payment infrastructure. The underfollowed discovery lane is strongest where education workflows are embedded inside broader payments companies: Flywire for higher-education tuition and cross-border payments, and Global Payments through TouchNet and Heartland ECSI. Corpay is a weaker but plausible second-order candidate tied to education-sector accounts-payable and supplier-payment automation rather than student-loan servicing itself.
